purpose: machine-readable offense-aware-defense ontology for securing wired and wireless networks and detecting attacks against them, encoding concrete defensive work-units (asset/threat mapping, segmentation, zero-trust, TLS/PKI, VPN, WPA2/WPA3 and 802.1X/EAP, WIDS/WIPS rogue-AP and deauth detection, IDS/IPS, NetFlow/anomaly and DNS-exfil detection, SIEM correlation, hardening/patching, purple-team validation, and incident response) as evaluable decisions for a knowledge-searcher meta-KB; adversary techniques are framed only as detection/hardening signals for authorized defense and education, not as operational intrusion playbooks.
assumptions: scope is defensive (offense-aware) network and wireless security; attacker techniques are encoded as detection/hardening signals only
no observed dataset or benchmark supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors
an enterprise network with both wired and wireless segments and a SOC is assumed
controls and detections operate under authorization and applicable privacy/legal constraints
exclusions: operational attack/exploit playbooks for unauthorized intrusion or evasion
endpoint/EDR, application-layer, and cloud-control-plane security except where they touch network controls
physical security and social engineering beyond their network detection signals

competency_questions.question: what assets, segments, and wireless infrastructure exist and what attack paths threaten them?
which attack paths are highest priority for detection and hardening?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from threat model and priority_order

competency_questions.question: how is the network segmented and access-controlled to contain lateral movement?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from segmentation, firewall, and zero-trust nodes

competency_questions.question: how is remote and per-request access authenticated and authorized?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from VPN and zero-trust nodes

competency_questions.question: how is transport trust (PKI, ciphers, revocation) managed?
which Wi-Fi protocols and authentication defend the wireless estate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from Wi-Fi protocol and 802.1X nodes

competency_questions.question: how are wireless attacks (evil-twin, deauth) detected and alarmed?
what network detection layers cover known and novel attacks and where do sensors sit?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from IDS, anomaly, and capture nodes

competency_questions.question: how are covert exfiltration channels such as DNS tunneling detected?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from DNS-exfil and anomaly nodes

competency_questions.question: how are multi-source signals correlated into prioritized, actionable alerts and responses?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from SIEM and IR nodes

competency_questions.question: how is the attack surface reduced through hardening and risk-based patching?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from hardening and patch nodes

competency_questions.question: how is detection and response coverage validated under authorization?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from purple-team and IR nodes

competency_questions.question: how are logs governed for integrity, time-sync, retention, and privacy?

glossary.definition: a rogue access point impersonating a legitimate SSID to capture credentials or traffic
802.11w Protected Management Frames, which authenticate management frames to resist deauth/disassoc spoofing
Simultaneous Authentication of Equals, the WPA3 handshake resisting offline dictionary attacks
fine-grained east-west isolation of workloads beyond coarse VLAN boundaries
an access model granting per-request authenticated, authorized access independent of network position
port-based network access control using EAP and a RADIUS authenticator
exported records of network flows used for behavioral and anomaly analysis
covert data transfer or C2 encoded in DNS queries and responses
wireless intrusion detection/prevention systems that monitor RF and 802.11 frames for attacks
correlation of BSSID/SSID/RF signals to flag spoofed access-point infrastructure
a baseline policy that denies all traffic except explicitly permitted flows
collaborative authorized adversary emulation to validate detection and response coverage

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established network and wireless security literature (Stallings & Brown, Computer Security: Principles and Practice; Gast, 802.11 Wireless Networks; Bejtlich, The Practice of Network Security Monitoring; Ferguson/Schneier/Kohno, Cryptography Engineering) and defensive practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Enumerate hosts, segments, wireless SSIDs/BSSIDs, services, and trust boundaries to produce the authoritative defensible network map.
contradictors: team that buys controls before mapping assets

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new segment, VLAN, AP, or unmanaged device appears on the network

pros.claim: a current inventory is the denominator every control and detection rule is scoped against
pros.example: unmonitored VLAN found before segmentation is designed

cons.claim: a stale or partial map silently leaves segments and rogue APs unmonitored
cons.example: detection tuned only for known subnets misses a shadow IoT VLAN

acceptance_tests: inventory reconciles discovery scan against CMDB with delta under threshold
every monitored segment maps to an owner and trust zone

nodes.definition: Model adversaries, entry points, and trust boundaries (offense-aware) so detection and hardening priorities map to realistic attack paths.
contradictors: analyst who lists CVEs without attack paths

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new attacker capability, entry point, or business-critical asset is identified

pros.claim: attack-path framing focuses limited detection budget on reachable, high-impact paths
pros.example: lateral-movement path to domain controllers prioritized over noisy edge alerts

cons.claim: an attacker-blind model defends the perimeter while internal pivots go unwatched
cons.example: flat network modeled as trusted, east-west traffic never inspected

failure_modes: model never revisited after topology change
acceptance_tests: each crown-jewel asset has at least one enumerated reachable attack path with a detection owner
trust zones are explicit and non-overlapping

nodes.definition: Design and enforce VLAN/subnet/microsegmentation boundaries that contain blast radius and constrain lateral movement.
contradictors: operator who flattens the network for convenience

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new trust zone, tenant, or compliance scope requires isolation

pros.claim: segmentation caps blast radius so one compromised host cannot reach crown jewels
pros.example: ransomware contained to one VLAN instead of the whole site

cons.claim: over-segmentation breaks legitimate flows and drives risky firewall exceptions
cons.example: clinicians blocked, so an any-any rule is added that erases the boundary

acceptance_tests: inter-zone matrix denies by default and every allow has a documented owner
no trunk port carries an unauthorized native VLAN

nodes.definition: Author, order, and review least-privilege firewall/ACL rule sets that enforce segmentation and default-deny posture.
contradictors: operator who appends permit-any at the top

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a segment policy changes or a rule-base audit finds shadowed/permissive rules

pros.claim: least-privilege ACLs make allowed flows explicit and auditable
pros.example: only TCP/443 to the app tier is permitted, all else denied and logged

cons.claim: rule sprawl creates shadowed and overly broad rules that quietly reopen paths
cons.example: an old any-any rule above a specific deny silently permits the traffic

acceptance_tests: rule base contains an explicit default-deny terminal rule
no enabled any-any allow rule exists without a documented exception

nodes.definition: Replace implicit network trust with per-request authenticated, authorized, encrypted access keyed to identity and device posture.
contradictors: team relying on VPN-equals-trusted model

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when remote access, BYOD, or cloud workloads expand the implicit-trust surface

pros.claim: per-request verification removes the flat trusted interior an intruder exploits
pros.example: stolen VPN creds still fail device-posture and step-up checks

cons.claim: poorly scoped policies block legitimate work and push users to shadow paths
cons.example: over-strict posture check locks out a whole field team mid-shift

failure_modes: policy gaps fall back to implicit trust
acceptance_tests: no application is reachable on network position alone without identity+authz
device posture is evaluated on every session, not just at login

nodes.definition: Manage certificate issuance, validation, cipher policy, and trust stores so transport encryption and authentication are sound and revocable.
contradictors: team that pins to expired or weak ciphers for compatibility

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a CA is compromised, a cipher is deprecated, or certificate lifetimes change

pros.claim: validated PKI gives authenticated, confidential transport and a revocation path
pros.example: compromised server cert revoked via OCSP before reissue

cons.claim: weak ciphers, unmanaged trust stores, or no revocation enable interception
cons.example: a private CA trusted everywhere lets a forged cert pass silently

acceptance_tests: only approved TLS versions and cipher suites are negotiated on monitored endpoints
every issued certificate has a tracked expiry and revocation path

nodes.definition: Configure and monitor VPN/tunnel termination with strong crypto, MFA, and split-tunnel policy for authenticated remote connectivity.
contradictors: admin who exposes a VPN portal without MFA

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when remote-access volume changes or a VPN appliance CVE is disclosed

pros.claim: strong tunnel crypto plus MFA authenticates remote users and protects traffic in transit
pros.example: credential-stuffing against the portal fails at the MFA step

cons.claim: unpatched VPN appliances and weak config are a top initial-access vector
cons.example: an unpatched gateway CVE gives an attacker an authenticated foothold

acceptance_tests: all VPN logons require MFA and are logged to the SIEM
negotiated tunnel ciphers match the approved crypto baseline

nodes.definition: Select and configure Wi-Fi security (WPA3 vs WPA2, SAE, PMF, transition modes) to maximize confidentiality and resist offline cracking.
contradictors: admin who keeps WPA2-only with PMF disabled

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when WPA3/PMF support changes or a handshake weakness is disclosed

pros.claim: WPA3-SAE plus PMF resists offline dictionary attacks and forged management frames
pros.example: SAE makes captured handshakes useless for offline cracking

cons.claim: WPA2 or mixed transition mode preserves crackable handshakes and deauth exposure
cons.example: transition mode lets a client be downgraded to WPA2 and captured

acceptance_tests: management frame protection is required on all corporate SSIDs
no production SSID permits WPA2-only without a documented exception

nodes.definition: Deploy 802.1X/EAP with RADIUS and server-certificate validation so wireless and wired ports authenticate identities, not just keys.
contradictors: admin who disables supplicant certificate validation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when EAP method, RADIUS trust, or supplicant validation policy changes

pros.claim: per-identity EAP-TLS with server validation defeats shared-key and evil-twin credential capture
pros.example: supplicant rejects a rogue RADIUS server with an untrusted certificate

cons.claim: unvalidated supplicants and weak EAP methods leak credentials to evil-twin APs
cons.example: PEAP without cert validation hands hashes to a fake AP

acceptance_tests: supplicants validate the RADIUS server certificate before sending credentials
only approved EAP methods are accepted by the RADIUS policy

nodes.definition: Detect unauthorized, rogue, and evil-twin access points by BSSID/SSID/RF anomaly correlation so spoofed infrastructure is alarmed.
contradictors: analyst who trusts SSID names as identity

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new SSID/BSSID, signal anomaly, or client-association anomaly is observed

pros.claim: BSSID/RF correlation flags spoofed APs that name-based trust would miss
pros.example: an evil twin reusing the corporate SSID on a foreign BSSID is alarmed

cons.claim: sensor gaps and noisy RF cause blind spots and alert fatigue
cons.example: a rogue AP in an unmonitored wing never triggers an alert

acceptance_tests: every authorized BSSID is allowlisted and deviations raise an alert
a planted test evil-twin is detected within the target window

nodes.definition: Detect deauthentication/disassociation floods and other Layer-2 wireless DoS as attack signals, leveraging PMF to harden against them.
contradictors: analyst who treats client drops as only RF noise

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when deauth/disassoc rates or handshake-recapture attempts spike

pros.claim: flagging deauth floods exposes handshake-capture and evil-twin staging attempts
pros.example: a deauth burst preceding a new evil-twin association is correlated and alarmed

cons.claim: without PMF the attack succeeds anyway and detection only confirms disruption
cons.example: clients forced off and recaptured before the alert is actioned

failure_modes: no PMF so detection is after-the-fact
thresholds too high to catch low-rate floods
acceptance_tests: abnormal deauth/disassoc rates raise an alert above an RF-noise baseline
PMF status is monitored and its absence is flagged

nodes.definition: Deploy and tune signature/policy IDS/IPS at choke points to detect and optionally block known malicious network patterns.
contradictors: operator who enables every signature inline at once

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new signatures, evasion techniques, or choke-point topology change

pros.claim: signatures at choke points give high-confidence detection of known TTPs and optional inline blocking
pros.example: a known C2 beacon signature fires at the egress choke point

cons.claim: signature-only detection misses novel and encrypted attacks and over-blocking breaks traffic
cons.example: an inline false positive drops production traffic during business hours

acceptance_tests: sensors cover every modeled crown-jewel attack path's choke point
inline-block rules have a tested rollback and change record

nodes.definition: Baseline NetFlow/IPFIX and behavioral traffic to detect anomalies, beaconing, scanning, and lateral movement that signatures miss.
contradictors: analyst who alerts on raw volume without a baseline

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when traffic baselines drift or a new lateral-movement pattern is hypothesized

pros.claim: behavioral baselines surface novel and encrypted-channel attacks signatures cannot see
pros.example: periodic beaconing to a new external host is flagged despite TLS

cons.claim: weak baselines and concept drift produce high false-positive rates and analyst fatigue
cons.example: seasonal traffic shift triggers a wave of benign anomaly alerts

failure_modes: encrypted east-west invisible to flow only
acceptance_tests: anomaly thresholds are derived from a documented baseline window, not fixed guesses
a simulated beacon is detected within the target window

nodes.definition: Detect DNS tunneling and exfiltration via query entropy, volume, NXDOMAIN, and rare-domain signals so covert channels are alarmed.
contradictors: analyst who ignores DNS as 'just resolution traffic'

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when DNS query patterns shift or a new tunneling tool/encoding is reported

pros.claim: entropy and volume signals expose DNS as a covert exfil and C2 channel attackers favor
pros.example: high-entropy subdomain bursts to one nameserver are flagged as tunneling

cons.claim: legitimate CDN/telemetry DNS noise and encrypted DNS (DoH) reduce visibility
cons.example: DoH routes queries around the resolver and hides the channel

failure_modes: benign high-entropy CDN domains cause noise
acceptance_tests: a simulated DNS-tunnel sample is detected by entropy/volume rules
encrypted-DNS egress is restricted to approved resolvers or flagged

nodes.definition: Aggregate network/wireless/identity telemetry and author correlation rules that turn multi-source signals into prioritized, actionable alerts.
contradictors: team that forwards logs but writes no correlation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new telemetry source is onboarded or a detection gap is identified

pros.claim: cross-source correlation converts weak single signals into high-confidence attack alerts
pros.example: rogue AP plus new VPN logon plus DNS-exfil correlate into one intrusion case

cons.claim: unparsed sources and rule sprawl create coverage gaps and alert overload
cons.example: a key firewall source is unparsed, so its rule silently never fires

acceptance_tests: every priority attack path maps to at least one correlation rule and an owner
each onboarded source is parsed and validated end-to-end before rules depend on it

nodes.definition: Engineer TAP/SPAN, full-packet/flow capture, and decryption-policy coverage so detection and forensics have the data they require.
contradictors: team that buys sensors but never solves visibility

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a monitored segment, encryption posture, or capture-retention policy changes

pros.claim: visibility at the right choke points is the precondition every sensor and forensic query depends on
pros.example: a TAP at the egress gives both IDS and incident responders ground truth

cons.claim: encrypted traffic, asymmetric routing, and SPAN drops create silent detection blind spots
cons.example: an oversubscribed SPAN port drops frames so detections miss the attack

acceptance_tests: each crown-jewel attack path has capture coverage at its choke point
SPAN/TAP loss is monitored and stays under a defined threshold

nodes.definition: Discover, prioritize, and remediate vulnerabilities in network and wireless infrastructure to shrink the exploitable attack surface.
contradictors: team that patches by calendar, ignoring exposure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a critical infrastructure CVE is disclosed or an exposure scan finds drift

pros.claim: risk-based patching closes the externally reachable, weaponized exposures attackers actually use
pros.example: an internet-facing VPN CVE is patched within the emergency window

cons.claim: blind calendar patching leaves reachable critical exposures open for weeks
cons.example: a perimeter device CVE waits for the monthly window and is exploited

acceptance_tests: externally reachable critical CVEs are remediated or mitigated within the defined SLA
every scanned exposure maps to an owner and a remediation decision

nodes.definition: Define and enforce secure configuration baselines for routers, switches, APs, and firewalls, detecting drift from the hardened standard.
contradictors: operator who leaves default credentials and telnet on

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a benchmark updates or configuration drift is detected from baseline

pros.claim: a hardened baseline removes default creds, weak protocols, and exposed mgmt planes attackers target
pros.example: SNMPv2 and telnet disabled, mgmt restricted to an out-of-band VLAN

cons.claim: unmanaged drift quietly reopens insecure services and management exposure
cons.example: a switch restored from old backup re-enables an insecure protocol

acceptance_tests: no managed device exposes default credentials or deprecated management protocols
baseline drift is detected and reported within the review cycle

nodes.definition: Validate detection and hardening with authorized adversary emulation and purple-team exercises, measuring coverage and time-to-detect.
contradictors: team that assumes a deployed rule actually fires

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a detection gap, false-negative, or new TTP requires re-validation

pros.claim: emulation proves which detections actually fire and surfaces silent false negatives
pros.example: an emulated evil-twin confirms the WIDS rule fires and pages the SOC

cons.claim: unscoped or unauthorized emulation can disrupt production or cross legal/ethical lines
cons.example: an over-broad deauth test knocks legitimate clients offline

acceptance_tests: every emulation runs under written authorization and a defined blast-radius boundary
each priority attack path has a measured detect/no-detect result

nodes.definition: Define authorized detection-to-containment playbooks (isolate, block, revoke, capture) that turn validated alerts into bounded response actions.
contradictors: team that improvises containment under live pressure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new attack class, containment capability, or business constraint changes response

pros.claim: pre-authorized playbooks make containment fast, bounded, and reversible under pressure
pros.example: an evil-twin alert auto-isolates the segment and pages on-call per playbook

cons.claim: over-aggressive automated containment can cause self-inflicted outages
cons.example: an auto-block on a false positive severs a clinical network mid-procedure

acceptance_tests: each playbook names a reversible containment action and an explicit escalation owner
destructive actions require a confirmation or human gate above a risk threshold

nodes.definition: Govern log integrity, retention, time synchronization, and privacy scope so detections and investigations rest on trustworthy, admissible data.
contradictors: team that keeps logs without integrity or sync

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when retention requirements, privacy law, or time-sync integrity change

pros.claim: tamper-evident, time-synced, retained logs make detections trustworthy and investigations defensible
pros.example: correlated events across sensors line up because clocks are NTP-synced

cons.claim: clock skew, gaps, or over-retention break correlation and create privacy/legal risk
cons.example: unsynced clocks misorder events and break the intrusion timeline

acceptance_tests: all detection sources are time-synchronized within a defined skew bound
retention meets policy and PII scope is documented and minimized

edges.why_related: the asset/topology map enumerates the entry points the threat model reasons over
edges.benefit_of_coupling: threat model scoped to real, current assets
edges.risk_of_conflict: modeling threats over a stale map misses live attack paths
edges.example: threat model omits a shadow VLAN absent from the inventory
edges.resolution_rule: complete the inventory before finalizing the threat model

edges.why_related: trust zones from the threat model define the segmentation boundaries
edges.benefit_of_coupling: segmentation contains the modeled attack paths
edges.risk_of_conflict: segmenting without attack paths wastes effort on low-value boundaries
edges.example: zones drawn around crown jewels identified in the model
edges.resolution_rule: finalize trust zones before locking segmentation

edges.why_related: the threat model identifies the implicit-trust surfaces zero-trust must remove
edges.benefit_of_coupling: zero-trust policy targets real trust assumptions
edges.risk_of_conflict: blanket zero-trust without modeling over-blocks low-risk flows
edges.example: implicit east-west trust flagged then replaced by per-request authz
edges.resolution_rule: prioritize zones by modeled risk before zero-trust rollout

edges.why_related: modeled attack paths set where IDS/IPS sensors and signatures matter most
edges.benefit_of_coupling: detection budget focused on reachable paths
edges.risk_of_conflict: signatures everywhere with no path priority drowns the SOC
edges.example: C2 signature placed at the egress path to crown jewels
edges.resolution_rule: derive sensor priority from attack paths before tuning

edges.why_related: wireless ingress in the threat model drives the required Wi-Fi protocol strength
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Wi-Fi baseline matches the wireless threat
edges.risk_of_conflict: weak protocol chosen because wireless ingress was underweighted
edges.example: WPA3+PMF mandated because guest-RF ingress is a modeled path
edges.resolution_rule: weight wireless ingress in the model before fixing Wi-Fi mode

edges.why_related: attack-path reachability prioritizes which vulnerabilities to remediate first
edges.benefit_of_coupling: patching ordered by exploitability and reachability
edges.risk_of_conflict: CVSS-only patching ignores actual exposure
edges.example: internet-facing VPN CVE prioritized over an internal low-reach bug
edges.resolution_rule: rank remediation by modeled reachability, not score alone

edges.why_related: segmentation boundaries define the firewall/ACL policy that enforces them
edges.benefit_of_coupling: rules implement designed boundaries
edges.risk_of_conflict: authoring rules before boundaries yields incoherent ACLs
edges.example: inter-zone matrix translated into default-deny ACLs
edges.resolution_rule: lock the segmentation matrix before writing firewall rules

edges.why_related: the inventory of TLS endpoints scopes certificate and cipher governance
edges.benefit_of_coupling: PKI policy covers all real endpoints
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged endpoints get orphaned certs and weak ciphers
edges.example: every TLS service in inventory mapped to a tracked certificate
edges.resolution_rule: inventory TLS endpoints before setting PKI policy

edges.why_related: VPN tunnels rely on PKI-issued certificates and the approved cipher baseline
edges.benefit_of_coupling: VPN crypto inherits validated trust
edges.risk_of_conflict: weak PKI undermines VPN authentication
edges.example: VPN gateway uses a tracked cert and approved cipher suite
edges.resolution_rule: establish PKI trust before standing up VPN termination

edges.why_related: zero-trust policy bounds what a VPN session may reach after connecting
edges.benefit_of_coupling: VPN connectivity no longer implies broad access
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating VPN as trusted reintroduces a flat interior
edges.example: post-VPN access still gated per-app by identity and posture
edges.resolution_rule: VPN provides transport only; authorization stays per-request

edges.why_related: EAP-TLS supplicant/server validation depends on PKI-issued certificates
edges.benefit_of_coupling: wireless auth gets cryptographic identity
edges.risk_of_conflict: unvalidated certs let evil twins harvest credentials
edges.example: RADIUS server cert chained to the managed CA and validated by clients
edges.resolution_rule: issue and validate RADIUS certs before enabling 802.1X

edges.why_related: the chosen Wi-Fi mode (WPA3-Enterprise) sets the EAP/802.1X requirements
edges.benefit_of_coupling: auth design matches the protocol baseline
edges.risk_of_conflict: mismatched mode and EAP method weakens both
edges.example: WPA3-Enterprise selected, so EAP-TLS with PMF is configured
edges.resolution_rule: fix the Wi-Fi security mode before designing EAP/RADIUS

edges.why_related: the authorized-AP inventory is the allowlist rogue detection compares against
edges.benefit_of_coupling: deviations from known BSSIDs become alertable
edges.risk_of_conflict: without an allowlist rogue detection cannot distinguish friend from foe
edges.example: an unknown BSSID broadcasting the corporate SSID is flagged
edges.resolution_rule: maintain the authorized-BSSID list before tuning rogue detection

edges.why_related: stronger Wi-Fi auth changes the likelihood and signature of evil-twin attempts
edges.benefit_of_coupling: detection focuses on the residual evil-twin vector
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring protocol strength misreads which spoofs can succeed
edges.example: PMF+SAE shifts attackers toward rogue infrastructure detection catches
edges.resolution_rule: tune rogue detection to the residual vector left by the protocol choice

edges.why_related: enabling PMF changes whether deauth floods succeed and how they are detected
edges.benefit_of_coupling: detection distinguishes blocked from successful floods
edges.risk_of_conflict: without PMF a flood succeeds before detection acts
edges.example: PMF-protected frames reduce deauth success and sharpen the anomaly signal
edges.resolution_rule: prefer PMF hardening; use deauth detection as the alerting layer

edges.why_related: deauth-flood detection often precedes and stages evil-twin association, so they are analyzed together
edges.benefit_of_coupling: correlated wireless attack chain
edges.risk_of_conflict: analyzing them separately misses the staged attack
edges.example: a deauth burst then a new BSSID association is one correlated case
edges.resolution_rule: correlate deauth and rogue-AP signals in one wireless detection view

edges.why_related: segmentation choke points are where IDS/IPS sensors are placed
edges.benefit_of_coupling: sensors sit on enforced boundaries
edges.risk_of_conflict: unsegmented networks have no natural inspection points
edges.example: an inter-zone choke point hosts the inline IPS
edges.resolution_rule: define choke points via segmentation before placing sensors

edges.why_related: topology defines where TAP/SPAN capture must exist for coverage
edges.benefit_of_coupling: visibility planned against real choke points
edges.risk_of_conflict: capture placed blindly leaves segments dark
edges.example: egress and inter-zone links get TAPs per the topology map
edges.resolution_rule: map topology before designing capture coverage

edges.why_related: segmentation determines which boundaries require capture and decryption policy
edges.benefit_of_coupling: capture scoped to enforced boundaries
edges.risk_of_conflict: capturing everywhere overwhelms storage and privacy scope
edges.example: only inter-zone and egress boundaries are tapped
edges.resolution_rule: scope capture to segmentation boundaries that matter

edges.why_related: IDS/IPS sensors require the packet visibility capture provides
edges.benefit_of_coupling: signatures see real traffic
edges.risk_of_conflict: sensors on lossy SPAN miss attacks
edges.example: IPS fed by a non-oversubscribed TAP, not a dropping SPAN
edges.resolution_rule: solve capture visibility before trusting sensor coverage

edges.why_related: flow analytics depend on flow/packet records the capture layer exports
edges.benefit_of_coupling: anomaly detection has complete flow data
edges.risk_of_conflict: flow gaps create silent anomaly blind spots
edges.example: IPFIX exported from the same choke points as packet capture
edges.resolution_rule: ensure flow export coverage before baselining anomalies

edges.why_related: signature and anomaly detection are complementary network-detection methods covering known vs novel patterns
edges.benefit_of_coupling: layered detection across known and unknown TTPs
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating them as interchangeable leaves a coverage gap
edges.example: signatures catch known C2; anomaly flags the novel beacon
edges.resolution_rule: run both layers; do not substitute one for the other

edges.why_related: DNS-exfil detection extends flow/behavioral baselining to the DNS channel
edges.benefit_of_coupling: covert DNS channels covered by the same baseline discipline
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring DNS leaves a favored exfil path open
edges.example: DNS query-volume baseline reuses the flow-baseline methodology
edges.resolution_rule: baseline flows before specializing DNS-exfil thresholds

edges.why_related: IDS/IPS alerts are a primary source the SIEM correlates
edges.benefit_of_coupling: single sensor alerts gain cross-source context
edges.risk_of_conflict: unparsed IDS alerts never enter correlation
edges.example: an IPS hit correlates with a new VPN logon in the SIEM
edges.resolution_rule: onboard and parse IDS alerts before building correlation rules

edges.why_related: anomaly detections feed the SIEM as correlatable signals
edges.benefit_of_coupling: weak anomaly signals strengthen via correlation
edges.risk_of_conflict: standalone anomalies stay low-confidence
edges.example: a beacon anomaly plus DNS-exfil signal correlate into one case
edges.resolution_rule: route anomaly outputs into correlation, not standalone alerting

edges.why_related: wireless rogue/evil-twin alerts are correlated with wired and identity events in the SIEM
edges.benefit_of_coupling: wireless and wired signals form one intrusion narrative
edges.risk_of_conflict: wireless alerts in a silo miss the broader attack
edges.example: an evil-twin alert correlates with anomalous internal logons
edges.resolution_rule: forward WIDS alerts to the SIEM for cross-domain correlation

edges.why_related: DNS-exfil signals are correlated with egress and host events in the SIEM
edges.benefit_of_coupling: exfil detection gains host and egress context
edges.risk_of_conflict: DNS alerts alone lack attribution
edges.example: high-entropy DNS bursts correlate with a single source host
edges.resolution_rule: feed DNS-exfil detections into SIEM correlation

edges.why_related: purple-team validation exercises the correlation rules to prove they fire
edges.benefit_of_coupling: correlation coverage is empirically tested
edges.risk_of_conflict: unexercised rules give false assurance
edges.example: an emulated intrusion confirms the multi-source rule pages the SOC
edges.resolution_rule: validate correlation rules via emulation before trusting coverage

edges.why_related: emulation validates that IDS/IPS signatures actually detect their target TTPs
edges.benefit_of_coupling: signature coverage measured, not assumed
edges.risk_of_conflict: a misdeployed signature silently never fires
edges.example: an emulated C2 beacon confirms the egress signature triggers
edges.resolution_rule: exercise signatures with emulation to confirm they fire

edges.why_related: authorized evil-twin emulation validates wireless rogue detection
edges.benefit_of_coupling: wireless detection proven under realistic spoofing
edges.risk_of_conflict: claimed WIDS coverage may be illusory
edges.example: a sanctioned test evil-twin confirms the WIDS alert and page
edges.resolution_rule: emulate rogue APs under authorization to validate detection

edges.why_related: prioritized SIEM alerts are the trigger inputs IR playbooks act on
edges.benefit_of_coupling: response is driven by correlated, prioritized signals
edges.risk_of_conflict: playbooks firing on raw noise cause outages
edges.example: a correlated intrusion case triggers the containment playbook
edges.resolution_rule: build correlation/prioritization before automating response

edges.why_related: segmentation boundaries are the levers playbooks use to isolate compromised zones
edges.benefit_of_coupling: containment is fast and bounded
edges.risk_of_conflict: without segments, isolation means full outage
edges.example: a playbook isolates one VLAN instead of the whole site
edges.resolution_rule: design segmentation before relying on it for containment

edges.why_related: firewall/ACL controls are the block actions playbooks invoke
edges.benefit_of_coupling: blocks are pre-authorized and reversible
edges.risk_of_conflict: ad-hoc blocks under pressure cause self-outages
edges.example: a playbook pushes a pre-approved egress block on the C2 domain
edges.resolution_rule: pre-stage reversible block rules before incident time

edges.why_related: captured data must be governed for integrity, retention, and privacy
edges.benefit_of_coupling: evidence is trustworthy and admissible
edges.risk_of_conflict: ungoverned capture is inadmissible and risky
edges.example: packet/flow records retained with tamper-evidence and PII scope
edges.resolution_rule: apply retention/integrity governance to captured data

edges.why_related: log integrity and time-sync governance bound how reliably the SIEM can correlate
edges.benefit_of_coupling: correlation rests on synced, intact logs
edges.risk_of_conflict: skewed clocks misorder correlated events
edges.example: NTP-synced sources let cross-sensor events line up
edges.resolution_rule: enforce time-sync and integrity before trusting correlation order

edges.why_related: hardening baselines and patch management both reduce attack surface and should be sequenced together
edges.benefit_of_coupling: fewer exposed services means fewer exploitable CVEs
edges.risk_of_conflict: patching without hardening leaves config-level exposures
edges.example: disabling telnet removes a class of CVEs from scope
edges.resolution_rule: harden configuration alongside risk-based patching

edges.why_related: the device inventory defines which devices the hardening baseline applies to
edges.benefit_of_coupling: no managed device escapes the baseline
edges.risk_of_conflict: uninventoried devices keep default configs
edges.example: every switch in inventory is checked against the baseline
edges.resolution_rule: inventory devices before enforcing hardening baselines

edges.why_related: identity-based zero-trust and coarse network segmentation compete as the primary access-control paradigm and can be over-invested redundantly
edges.benefit_of_coupling: defense-in-depth when balanced
edges.risk_of_conflict: duplicated, conflicting controls waste effort and confuse policy ownership
edges.example: teams argue whether east-west control lives in VLAN ACLs or per-request authz
edges.resolution_rule: use segmentation for blast-radius containment and zero-trust for access decisions; assign each a non-overlapping role

edges.why_related: inline IPS blocking and firewall deny policy both drop traffic and can double-drop or mask each other, creating availability tension
edges.benefit_of_coupling: layered blocking when coordinated
edges.risk_of_conflict: uncoordinated inline blocks cause hard-to-diagnose outages
edges.example: an IPS auto-block and a firewall rule both drop a flow, hiding the true cause
edges.resolution_rule: the firewall owns coarse default-deny; IPS inline-block is reserved for high-confidence signatures with rollback

edges.why_related: encrypted DNS (DoH/DoT) advances transport privacy but reduces DNS-exfil visibility, a privacy-vs-detection tension
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balanced when egress DNS is constrained to approved resolvers
edges.risk_of_conflict: unrestricted encrypted DNS blinds exfil detection
edges.example: DoH bypasses the resolver, hiding tunneling from entropy analysis
edges.resolution_rule: permit encrypted DNS only to approved, logged resolvers so privacy and detection coexist

conflict_axes.trigger: encryption and privacy scoping reduce the traffic visibility detection depends on
resolution_order: identify the minimum visibility each priority detection needs
constrain encrypted egress to approved logged paths
minimize captured PII to what detection and law require
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: detection gets the minimum visibility required for crown-jewel paths; privacy/encryption dominates beyond that minimum
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a detection requires decrypting regulated personal data
conflict_axes.example: DoH improves privacy but hides DNS tunneling unless egress is constrained to logged resolvers

conflict_axes.trigger: automated inline blocking or containment can drop legitimate production traffic
resolution_order: restrict inline block to high-confidence signatures
require tested rollback for inline rules
gate destructive containment behind a risk threshold
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: prevention dominates for high-confidence, low-false-positive signatures; availability dominates for uncertain ones, which alert-only
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an inline block would affect a safety-critical or clinical network
conflict_axes.example: an inline IPS false positive severs production traffic during business hours

conflict_axes.trigger: tighter segmentation and per-request authz break legitimate workflows and drive risky exceptions
resolution_order: map required business flows first
grant least-privilege allows with owners
review exceptions on a fixed cycle
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: containment dominates by default; documented, owned, time-bounded exceptions are allowed for verified business need
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an exception would create an any-any path across a trust boundary
conflict_axes.example: clinicians blocked, so an any-any rule is added that erases the boundary

conflict_axes.trigger: signatures are precise but miss novel attacks while anomaly detection is broad but noisy
resolution_order: use signatures for known high-confidence TTPs
use anomaly for novel/encrypted behavior
correlate both before paging
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: neither dominates; layer them and require correlation to suppress anomaly false positives
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: anomaly false-positive rate exceeds analyst capacity
conflict_axes.example: signatures catch known C2 while anomaly flags the novel beacon

conflict_axes.trigger: mandating WPA3/PMF/EAP-TLS can lock out legacy clients still on the network
resolution_order: inventory client capabilities
isolate legacy clients on a constrained SSID
retire or upgrade incompatible clients on a deadline
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: strong protocol dominates for corporate SSIDs; legacy compatibility is confined to an isolated, monitored segment with an end-of-life date
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a safety-critical legacy device cannot support PMF
conflict_axes.example: transition mode left on for compatibility lets a client be downgraded to WPA2 and captured

conflict_axes.trigger: finite budget forces a tradeoff between hardening/prevention and monitoring/detection
resolution_order: fund prevention for high-irreversibility crown-jewel paths
fund detection where prevention is incomplete
rebalance using purple-team gap results
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: prevention dominates for irreversible/high-impact assets; detection dominates where residual risk remains after feasible prevention
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a crown-jewel path has neither adequate prevention nor detection
conflict_axes.example: all budget spent on a SIEM while an unpatched perimeter device stays exploitable

conflict_axes.trigger: automated containment is fast but can act on false positives without human context
resolution_order: automate only validated high-confidence detections
require human gate for destructive/irreversible actions
review automated actions post-incident
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: automation dominates for reversible, high-confidence containment; human review dominates for destructive or low-confidence actions
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: automated action would be irreversible or hit a safety-critical system
conflict_axes.example: an auto-block on a false positive severs a clinical network mid-procedure

conflict_axes.trigger: maximizing coverage raises alert volume until analysts miss true positives
resolution_order: prioritize coverage of crown-jewel paths
tune and correlate to cut false positives
measure precision via emulation before expanding
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: coverage dominates for priority attack paths; precision dominates elsewhere to preserve analyst attention
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: true-positive miss rate rises due to alert overload
conflict_axes.example: a seasonal traffic shift floods the queue and a real beacon alert is buried

conflict_axes.trigger: emergency patching or cipher changes risk breaking production services
resolution_order: assess reachability and exploit availability
stage changes with rollback
fast-track only externally reachable weaponized exposures
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: speed dominates for reachable, weaponized exposures; stability dominates for internal low-reach issues patched on cycle
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an emergency change would disrupt a safety-critical service
conflict_axes.example: a perimeter CVE waits for the monthly window and is exploited first

edge_cases.trigger: a broad any-any exception is added to fix a broken legitimate flow
edge_cases.example: an any-any rule above a specific deny reopens cross-zone traffic
edge_cases.detection_method: diff the live rule base against the approved inter-zone matrix and flag any-any allows
resolution: replace with a scoped allow and an owner
schedule the exception for review and removal

edge_cases.trigger: a SPAN port is oversubscribed and silently drops frames
edge_cases.failure_mode: detection blind spot at a crown-jewel choke point
edge_cases.example: an IPS on a dropping SPAN misses the attack frames
edge_cases.detection_method: monitor capture-interface drop counters against a loss threshold
resolution: move to a dedicated TAP
rebalance or filter the mirrored traffic

edge_cases.trigger: detection or clients trust an SSID by name rather than authenticated infrastructure
edge_cases.example: a fake AP reusing the corporate SSID harvests PEAP credentials
edge_cases.detection_method: alert on the authorized SSID broadcast from an unauthorized BSSID and verify supplicant cert validation is enforced
resolution: enforce server-certificate validation on supplicants
allowlist authorized BSSIDs and alert deviations

edge_cases.trigger: hosts use encrypted DNS (DoH) to an external resolver
edge_cases.example: DoH routes high-entropy queries around the monitored resolver
edge_cases.detection_method: flag DNS-over-HTTPS egress to non-approved resolvers via flow/TLS-SNI analysis
resolution: restrict DoH to approved logged resolvers
block or alert on unapproved encrypted-DNS egress

edge_cases.trigger: a deauth flood hits an SSID without management-frame protection
edge_cases.failure_mode: clients forced off and handshakes captured before response
edge_cases.example: deauth frames disconnect clients and a handshake is recaptured for offline cracking
edge_cases.detection_method: alert on abnormal deauth/disassoc rate and on SSIDs lacking PMF
resolution: enable PMF on the affected SSID
raise the deauth-rate alert and correlate with new associations

edge_cases.trigger: log sources drift out of time synchronization
edge_cases.failure_mode: correlated events misordered and the intrusion timeline breaks
edge_cases.example: unsynced clocks make a cause appear after its effect
edge_cases.detection_method: monitor per-source clock skew against an NTP reference and alert beyond a bound
resolution: restore NTP sync on the drifting source
re-normalize timestamps before correlation

edge_cases.trigger: a forwarded log source is not parsed or silently dropped
edge_cases.failure_mode: a correlation rule never fires despite apparent coverage
edge_cases.example: a firewall feed parses to null fields so its rule is dead
edge_cases.detection_method: end-to-end heartbeat and parse-success monitoring per source
resolution: fix the parser/field mapping
add a synthetic-event test for each rule's required source

edge_cases.trigger: an internet-facing VPN appliance has an unpatched critical CVE
edge_cases.failure_mode: authenticated foothold via a known exploit
edge_cases.example: a known gateway CVE is exploited before the monthly patch window
edge_cases.detection_method: continuously map exposed VPN versions against CVE feeds and exploit availability
resolution: apply emergency patch or mitigation within the SLA
tighten access and watch the gateway for exploitation signals

edge_cases.trigger: an inline IPS or automated containment acts on a false positive
edge_cases.failure_mode: self-inflicted outage of legitimate production traffic
edge_cases.example: an inline block drops a clinical workflow mid-procedure
edge_cases.detection_method: track inline-block actions against an availability SLO and confidence score
resolution: roll back via the tested procedure
downgrade the uncertain signature to alert-only

edge_cases.trigger: supplicants are configured without server-certificate validation
edge_cases.failure_mode: credentials handed to a rogue RADIUS/evil-twin
edge_cases.example: PEAP without cert validation leaks hashes to a fake AP
edge_cases.detection_method: audit supplicant profiles for enforced CA/server-name validation
resolution: push profiles that require server-cert validation
pin the RADIUS server certificate/CA

edge_cases.trigger: a device is restored or onboarded with default credentials or deprecated protocols
edge_cases.example: a switch restored from old backup re-enables telnet and a default login
edge_cases.detection_method: baseline-drift scan for default credentials and deprecated management protocols
resolution: enforce the hardening baseline on the device
rotate credentials and disable insecure protocols

workflow.objective: establish the authoritative network map and the offense-aware threat model that scopes all defense
acceptance_tests: every monitored segment maps to an owner and trust zone
each crown jewel has at least one enumerated attack path
workflow.do_first_because: the inventory and threat model are the highest-coupling foundations every later control inherits

workflow.objective: design containment via segmentation, enforce it with least-privilege rules, and replace implicit trust with per-request access
acceptance_tests: inter-zone matrix denies by default with owned allows
no application is reachable on network position alone
workflow.do_first_because: segmentation is a high-irreversibility foundation that downstream detection and response depend on

workflow.objective: establish PKI/cipher trust and authenticated, MFA-protected remote access
acceptance_tests: only approved TLS versions/ciphers negotiate
all VPN logons require MFA and are logged
workflow.do_first_because: PKI trust is a prerequisite for VPN and enterprise Wi-Fi authentication downstream

workflow.objective: select strong Wi-Fi protocols and deploy validated 802.1X/EAP authentication
acceptance_tests: PMF required on corporate SSIDs
supplicants validate the RADIUS server certificate
workflow.do_first_because: wireless protocol strength bounds the residual attack surface wireless detection must cover

workflow.objective: engineer capture visibility and reduce attack surface via hardening baselines and risk-based patching
acceptance_tests: each crown-jewel path has capture coverage at its choke point
externally reachable critical CVEs remediated within SLA
workflow.do_first_because: capture visibility is the precondition every sensor and detection depends on

workflow.objective: deploy layered network detection: signatures, flow/anomaly baselines, and DNS-exfil signals
acceptance_tests: sensors cover every modeled crown-jewel choke point
a simulated beacon is detected within the target window
workflow.do_first_because: network detection layers feed the correlation and validation that follow

workflow.objective: deploy WIDS/WIPS for rogue/evil-twin and deauth-flood detection
acceptance_tests: every authorized BSSID is allowlisted and deviations alert
a planted test evil-twin is detected within the window
workflow.do_first_because: wireless detections are required inputs to cross-domain SIEM correlation

workflow.objective: correlate multi-source telemetry into prioritized alerts on governed, time-synced, retained logs
acceptance_tests: every priority attack path maps to a correlation rule and owner
all detection sources are time-synchronized within the skew bound
workflow.do_first_because: correlation must exist and rest on governed logs before response is automated

workflow.objective: validate detection and hardening with authorized adversary emulation and measure time-to-detect
acceptance_tests: every emulation runs under written authorization and a blast-radius boundary
each priority path has a measured detect/no-detect result
workflow.do_first_because: validation must confirm detections fire before response and lock decisions rely on them

workflow.objective: finalize authorized detection-to-containment playbooks and gate hard-lock on validation and human review
acceptance_tests: each playbook names a reversible containment action and an escalation owner
destructive actions require a human gate above the risk threshold
workflow.do_first_because: response playbooks may hard-lock only after validation, dependency, and human-review gates pass

priority_rationale.notes: root map every control is scoped against
enforces segmentation; block lever for response
trust root for VPN and EAP auth
covers a favored covert exfil channel

dominance_rules.trigger: a deadline pressures shipping a control or detection before its risk review
dominance_rules.rule: high-risk defensive changes must pass risk review before deployment
dominance_rules.required_action: block deployment until risk review and acceptance tests pass
dominance_rules.example: rushing an inline IPS block live without a rollback plan

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value detection is requested before its prerequisite visibility exists
dominance_rules.required_action: sequence the prerequisite (capture/segmentation) before the dependent control
dominance_rules.example: deploying IDS before solving capture visibility

dominance_rules.trigger: a numeric risk score is asserted with more precision than the heuristic basis supports
dominance_rules.rule: the evidence label governs; do not over-state certainty
dominance_rules.required_action: keep heuristic labels and widen uncertainty rather than fake precision
dominance_rules.example: claiming an observed detection rate with no measured data

dominance_rules.trigger: a control is proposed for hard-lock before detection validation runs
dominance_rules.required_action: require purple-team validation before any hard-lock
dominance_rules.example: hard-locking IR playbooks before emulation confirms detections fire

dominance_rules.trigger: an automated containment action would be irreversible or hit a safety-critical system
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for destructive or irreversible actions
dominance_rules.required_action: gate the action behind explicit human approval
dominance_rules.example: auto-isolating a clinical network on a single low-confidence alert

dominance_rules.trigger: an exception is requested that would flatten a segmentation boundary
dominance_rules.rule: containment dominates; exceptions must be scoped, owned, and time-bounded
dominance_rules.required_action: replace any-any requests with least-privilege owned allows
dominance_rules.example: adding an any-any rule to fix a broken flow

dominance_rules.trigger: a crown-jewel path is irreversible-impact and prevention is feasible
dominance_rules.rule: prevention dominates detection for high-irreversibility crown-jewel paths
dominance_rules.required_action: fund prevention first; use detection for residual risk
dominance_rules.example: relying only on a SIEM alert to protect an unpatched perimeter device

dominance_rules.trigger: detection requests visibility beyond the minimum needed, into regulated data
dominance_rules.rule: privacy dominates beyond the minimum visibility a priority detection requires
dominance_rules.required_action: scope capture and decryption to the documented minimum
dominance_rules.example: decrypting regulated personal traffic for a low-priority detection

dominance_rules.trigger: output structure conflicts with adding explanatory prose
dominance_rules.required_action: emit only schema-valid JSON; move rationale into defined fields
dominance_rules.example: adding comments to the KB that break strict parsing

dominance_rules.trigger: a defensive claim is stronger than its source supports
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade or remove claims beyond SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR support
dominance_rules.example: labeling a heuristic prior as an observed benchmark result

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete the asset inventory before selecting controls
anti_rework_rules.rationale: controls scoped to a stale map leave segments unmonitored
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: control purchased before its target assets are mapped
anti_rework_rules.example: buying a WIDS before inventorying the wireless estate

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the threat model before tuning detection
anti_rework_rules.rationale: detection without attack paths wastes budget and drowns the SOC
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: signatures enabled everywhere with no path priority
anti_rework_rules.example: turning on every IDS signature before mapping attack paths

anti_rework_rules.rule: lock the segmentation matrix before writing firewall rules
anti_rework_rules.rationale: rules authored before boundaries become incoherent and shadowed
anti_rework_rules.example: writing permit rules before the inter-zone matrix exists

anti_rework_rules.rule: establish PKI trust before VPN and 802.1X depend on it
anti_rework_rules.rationale: weak PKI silently undermines every authentication built on it
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: VPN/EAP stood up on unvalidated certificates
anti_rework_rules.example: enabling EAP-TLS before the RADIUS cert chain is validated

anti_rework_rules.rule: solve capture visibility before trusting sensor coverage
anti_rework_rules.rationale: sensors on lossy capture create silent blind spots
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: IPS placed on an oversubscribed dropping SPAN
anti_rework_rules.example: deploying IDS before confirming the TAP is lossless

anti_rework_rules.rule: set the Wi-Fi protocol baseline before tuning wireless detection
anti_rework_rules.rationale: detection tuned to the wrong residual vector misreads which spoofs succeed
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: rogue detection tuned before PMF/SAE decisions
anti_rework_rules.example: tuning deauth detection before deciding whether PMF is enabled

anti_rework_rules.rule: parse and validate each telemetry source before correlation depends on it
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an unparsed source makes a correlation rule silently dead
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: rule depends on a feed that parses to null
anti_rework_rules.example: writing a correlation rule on a firewall feed that was never parsed

anti_rework_rules.rule: enforce time synchronization before trusting correlation order
anti_rework_rules.rationale: clock skew misorders correlated events and breaks timelines
anti_rework_rules.example: building an attack timeline on unsynced log sources

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate detections via emulation before automating response
anti_rework_rules.rationale: automating response on unexercised detections risks false-positive outages
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: playbooks armed on rules never confirmed to fire
anti_rework_rules.example: auto-containment wired to a correlation rule that was never tested

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete human review before hard-locking irreversible response
anti_rework_rules.rationale: hard-locking before review embeds unreviewed irreversible actions
anti_rework_rules.example: locking an auto-isolation playbook before a human approves its blast radius

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or detection-validation reports a failure
iteration_protocol.detection: compare validation_report checks and purple-team results to thresholds
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.trigger: multiple defects or detection gaps are open
iteration_protocol.detection: rank by risk_score and attack-path reachability
action: score defects by risk and reachability
acceptance_tests: highest-risk reachable gap is first

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-coupling node or locked control would change
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents via edges and dependencies
acceptance_tests: all dependents identified

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is assigned for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to repair_routing subsystem
acceptance_tests: repair owner recorded
no regression in priority-path coverage

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence or a measured detection result arrives
acceptance_tests: posterior recomputed within tolerance

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is irreversible, safety-critical, or exceeds risk threshold
iteration_protocol.detection: check risk_score and irreversibility against human-review thresholds
acceptance_tests: approver and risk acceptance recorded

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new KB or detection version is proposed for release
iteration_protocol.detection: compare against the prior version coverage and validation
action: diff coverage and validation against prior
acceptance_tests: no loss of priority-path coverage

human_review_required_for: decrypting regulated personal data for detection
emergency changes to a safety-critical network

an internet-facing VPN appliance has a weaponized CVE
a deauth burst disconnects clients on a corporate SSID
authorized emulation tests whether deployed rules fire

version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked control or playbook change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream control changes
